Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Check out the complete list of scoring leaders here.

Sept. 18: Josh Allen puts league on notice with 40-point night

by Adam Rank

We had one of the highest-scoring Week 1s in NFL history last week. There was no way we could possibly top that, yeah? Well, I've got news for you, the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions accepted the challenge and put up massive numbers on Thursday night.

Josh Allen led the way with more than 40 points to get your week started. We went into the draft season saying Allen was in his own tier and he's proving it early on. Allen had over 300 total yards and five total touchdowns. Allen is the third player in NFL history with nine total touchdowns and no turnovers in his team's first two games of the season. The other two were Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013. Both went on to win MVP. Manning's Broncos also set the NFL record for most points in the season.

The Bills are the first team to record 35 points and more than 400 yards of offense in both of their first two games of the season since the Packers in 2020. The Bills have also scored five touchdowns in five red zone drives.

My guy Tristan H. Cockcroft pointed out during our in-game group chat that Allen broke the record for most fantasy points scored in the first two weeks of the season. Breaking the record of ... Ryan Fitzpatrick, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers version (as noted by Field Yates, who knew the answer to Tristan's trivia question).

Our group chat also had an interesting conversation about James Cook III. Is he a trade-high candidate because it's Josh Allen's offense, including goal-line carries -- or do you try to get more shares of Cook, if possible? Put me in the convo for more shares. I want as much of this Bills offense as possible. Especially if D.J. Moore is going to miss time. (Note: Moore is considered day-to-day)

Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir both had six targets. Joshua Palmer had a 43-yard TD reception on his lone target.

Dalton Kincaid had seven receptions for 95 yards and one receiving touchdown. He now has 22

articles.headline: Flores Jr. hits go-ahead, 2-run homer in 8th as Pirates rally for 4-3 win and series sweep of Royals
articles.description: — Rafael Flores Jr. hit the go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to help the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 4-3 win over the Kansas City Royals on Sunday and complete a series sweep.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- — Rafael Flores Jr. hit the go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to help the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 4-3 win over the Kansas City Royals on Sunday and complete a series sweep.


              After Ryan O’Hearn led off with a single to center, Flores sent a slider from Nate Pearson (2-3) into the left-field bleachers for his 10th homer this season.


              Pittsburgh rallied with a two-run homer in the eighth for a second straight day. Brandon Lowe had his 33rd of the season in a 6-5 win Saturday.


              Carmen Mlodzinki (8-7) got the win. He allowed two runs and three hits in three innings. The reliever gave up a pinch-hit, two-run home run to Vinnie Pasquantino that gave Kansas City a 3-2 lead with two outs in the seventh.


              Mason Montgomery earned his 16th save. He retired the first two batters in the ninth before Luke Maile hit a double and took third on a fielding error by Jake Mangum. Montgomery got Isaac Collins to fly out to right to strand Maile.


              The Royals went ahead 1-0 in the first inning with three straight singles off Lake Bachar. Bobby Witt Jr. beat out a groundball to second baseman Lowe. He moved to third on a single to right from Jac Caglianone and scored when Perez shot one through the middle of the infield. 


              Oneil Cruz tied it on his 20th home run of the season, starting the fourth inning with a drive to center field off a curveball left hanging in the middle of the zone by Wacha.


              Spencer Horwitz put the Pirates up 2-1 with a bloop single to center off Michael Wacha that drove in O’Hearn with two outs in the sixth.


              Up next 
              Royals: LHP Daniel Lynch IV (6-5, 3.29 ERA) is in line to start Tuesday to open a three-game home series against the White Sox. LHP Anthony Kay (9-9, 4.41 ERA) is the probable starter for Chicago.


              Pirates: RHP Jared Jones (4-6, 4.17 ERA) is expected to start Tuesday in the first of a three-game series against the Cardinals. RHP Andre Pallante (12-7, 3.70 ERA) will take the mound for St. Louis.


              ------ 


              AP MLB: https://apnews.com/hub/mlb

articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off Thursday night with an impressive win by the Bills over the Lions in the first regular-season game at Highmark Stadium. In the early window Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots solidified their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. In Baltimore, the Saints launched a late comeback for the second straight week -- but this time, they came out on top.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

NO-BAL | CAR-ATL | PIT-NE

Catch up on Thursday's game:

DET-BUF

New Orleans 24, Baltimore 17

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Saints

How will the Saints fix their slow starts? The Saints put themselves into an early hole for the second week in a row, but it worked out this time with some second-half heroics. The slow starts on offense are becoming a pattern under coach Kellen Moore. According to ESPN Research, this is the Saints' fourth straight game without putting up points in the first quarter. It's their second-longest streak in the past 10 seasons and the longest since they went five straight games in 2021.

Trend to watch: According to ESPN Research, the Saints were 5-of-8 on third-and-long conversions (at least 7 yards) before scoring the go-ahead touchdown at the end of the game. The Saints might start slow, but they've already shown an ability in the past few weeks to make key conversions, particularly between Tyler Shough, Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: vs. Raiders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Ravens

Why do the Ravens continue to lose leads in the fourth quarter? Baltimore thought it would change its fortune late in games by changing head coaches. But just like it did so many times under John Harbaugh, the Ravens failed to finish in the fourth quarter in Jesse Minter's second game. In Harbaugh's last five seasons with Baltimore, the Ravens lost an NFL-worst 14 games when leading through three quarters. Baltimore gave up two touchdown drives after entering the fourth quarter with a 17-9 lead Sunday. It will be debated whether Shough crossed the goal line on fourth-and-goal, but the Ravens had their chances to win. Quarterback Lamar Jackson's interception with 13 seconds left ended the game.

Trend to watch: With No. 1 target Zay Flowers out with a hamstring injury, Rashod Bateman stepped up to break out of a rut. He finished with seven catches for 88 yards, the fourth most of his career. This ended a streak of seven straight games of less than 50 yards receiving. Bateman also made a leaping 22-yard grab in the end zone, marking his first touchdown since Oct. 3

articles.headline: Blue Jays' Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (back) exits early at Texas
articles.description: Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. exited early Sunday against the Rangers because of left lower back tightness.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. exited early from Sunday's series finale at the Texas Rangers because of left lower back tightness.

Guerrero was replaced in the field in the bottom of the fourth inning. Myles Straw entered the game in left field, while Josh Smith moved from there to third base. Kazuma Okamoto then switched from third to first base, where Guerrero was playing.

Guerrero had a single in the first inning and hit a comebacker to Jacob deGrom in the third.

Guerrero is hitting .263 with nine homers and 56 RBIs in 141 games this season.

Okamoto played only one inning at first base. He moved back to third after Charles McAdoo pinch-hit for Smith in the fifth inning and then entered the game at first base.

articles.headline: Sánchez earns 18th win to take over major league lead as the Phillies beat the Mets 7-2
articles.description: — Cristopher Sánchez earned his major league-leading 18th win Sunday, leading the Philadelphia Phillies to a 7-2 victory over the New York Mets.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Cristopher Sánchez earned his major league-leading 18th win Sunday, leading the Philadelphia Phillies to a 7-2 victory over the New York Mets.


              The Phillies (86-70), who salvaged a split of the four-game series, entered Sunday in the third National League wild-card spot, one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four games clear of the Arizona Diamondbacks.


              Sánchez surrendered six hits — including Bo Bichette’s sixth-inning homer — and struck out six over 6 1/3 innings as he snapped a tie with the Boston Red Sox’s Sonny Gray for the big league lead in wins.


              The last Phillies pitcher to lead the majors in wins was Steve Carlton with 23 in 1982.


              Justin Crawford had a three-run triple and Luis Arraez finished with two RBI. Alec Bohm and Trea Turner each had run-scoring hits. Kyle Schwarber tied a career high with four walks.


              Rookie Jonah Tong (2-2) gave up four runs and struck out five in 4 2/3 innings for the last-place Mets, who finished 36-45 at home — their worst record at Citi Field since the 2013 team went 33-48.


              The Mets drew 2,712,120 fans this season, a drop of 5,870 fans per game from last season — the steepest decline in the majors.


              Brett Baty added a pinch-hit RBI single.


              Despite a rainy forecast and the postponement of a ceremony honoring retiring Mets radio broadcaster Howie Rose, the game began on time and wasn’t interrupted. The crowd of 33,611 cheered and chanted Rose’s name after “Hello, Goodbye” by The Beatles played in the eighth.


              Up next
              Phillies: Open their final homestand Tuesday, when RHP Zack Wheeler (13-5, 2.99 ERA) starts against the NL Central champion Milwaukee Brewers, who haven’t announced a starter.


              Mets: LHP Sean Manaea (5-7, 4.74 ERA) starts Tuesday against the Texas Rangers, who haven’t announced a starter.


              ------


              AP MLB: https://apnews.com/hub/mlb
